chunks: And Wahb ibn Wahb narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, peace be upon him, who said:
ʿAlī, peace be upon him, said: “There is no harm in advancing payment for what is weighed in exchange for what is measured, and for what is measured in exchange for what is weighed.”

key_terms.عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam ʿAlī, peace be upon him, the speaker of the ruling
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible
key_terms.يُسْلَفَ: to be advanced in payment; to be transacted as salam
key_terms.يُكَالُ: that which is sold by measure
key_terms.يُوزَنُ: that which is sold by weight

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to make an advance-payment sale between weighed goods and measured goods?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling permitting salam transactions between goods that are sold by weight and goods that are sold by measure. It indicates the permissibility of advance payment in such exchanges within the framework of Islamic commercial law.
